quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: When can you cross solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During daylight hours only.
At any time.
When making turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: Solid yellow lines cannot be crossed. You can only cross a solid yellow line when you are turning.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates, you should:

options.text: Cross the tracks immediately and as quickly as possible.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Prepare to yield to any train at the crossing.
Speed up to beat any oncoming train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to yield to any train at the crossing.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to any train before crossing railroad tracks. Do not cross until your entire vehicle can fit on the other side. Do not shift gears while crossing.

questions.question: When visibility is poor, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Reduce your speed.
Turn on your windshield wipers.
Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Your first action when visibility decreases should be to slow down.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Narrow bridge ahead.
Lane ends or roadway narrows ahead.
Industrial area.
Freeway on-ramp ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends or roadway narrows ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow background. This sign warns that a lane is ending or the road is narrowing.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow arrow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop, if it is safe to do so.
Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Have the right-of-way and expect oncoming traffic to stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, what should you do?

options.text: Always insist on the right-of-way over a vehicle when using a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
Enter a crosswalk at any time because drivers must stop.
Use crosswalks only if they are convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. A vehicle that is close may not have time to stop.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway and children are playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children you are moving.
Sound your horn so the children hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to check the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to check the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Get out of your vehicle and check behind it before backing up. Do not rely only on your mirrors, especially with children nearby.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Go slowly while waiting for an opening.
Speed up faster than the traffic.
Turn on your hazard lights until safely on the freeway.
Speed up to match the freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to freeway speed so you can blend in smoothly. You must yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: In winter, what happens to overpasses and bridges?

options.text: They are affected the same way as other roadways.
They freeze after the rest of the roads.
They thaw out before the rest of the roads.
They freeze before the rest of the roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: They freeze before the rest of the roads.
questions.explanation: In winter, overpasses and bridges freeze before other roads and stay icy longer. Be extra careful when driving on them.

questions.question: If a car with high beams comes toward you, where should you look?

options.text: Either side
The center
The right side
The left side

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and lets you see enough to stay on your course until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: Your vehicle's accelerator sticks open while driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Press the brakes hard.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Turn off the ignition. Be careful not to lock the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the ignition. Be careful not to lock the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: When the accelerator sticks, the engine keeps running at high speed even if you lift your foot off the gas. Turn off the ignition carefully. Only move the switch enough to stop the engine. Do not turn it so far that the steering wheel locks. Then apply the brakes and move to a safe area.

questions.question: What is the best way to stay safe when backing up your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn right before you shift into reverse.
Walk around the back of the vehicle to check for obstacles before getting in the driver's seat.
Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.
Turn up the car radio before backing up so people nearby notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk around the back of the vehicle to check for obstacles before getting in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: It is hard to see behind your vehicle when backing up. Always walk to the back and look for children and small objects before you get in and back up.

questions.question: What are regulatory signs?

options.text: They are placed everywhere there is danger.
They tell you what you must or must not do.
They are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
They warn you about school zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: They tell you what you must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black text on a white background. They show what drivers must or must not do in an area. They display speed limits, say whether you can or cannot pass, or explain other driving rules.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to the lane you came from.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the lane you came from.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane that is closest to where you came from. This keeps you from crossing other lanes and is safer.

questions.question: What does a speed restriction sign show?

options.text: You can ignore it if the weather is rainy, snowy, or icy.
It has a triangular shape.
It is blue with black letters.
A recommended safe speed for a curve or turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: A recommended safe speed for a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: Speed signs for curves and turns show a suggested speed. Even if you feel safe driving faster in good weather, you must slow down in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: What do fluorescent yellow-green signs indicate?

options.text: School zones.
Hospitals.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Fluorescent yellow-green signs warn about pedestrians, bicycles, and schools. Drive carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always stop completely at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. You must come to a full stop if traffic requires it.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
They rarely use their headlights.
Motorcycle riders are less skilled than other drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and easy to miss. They can hide in your blind spot. It is hard to judge how far away they are or how fast they are going. Always be alert around motorcycles.

questions.question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left, where should you look?

options.text: Over your right shoulder.
In your side mirror.
Over your left shoulder.
In your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left shoulder.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a red traffic light.
You may turn in the direction the arrow points.
Traffic in the arrow's direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a red traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow has the same meaning as a circular red traffic light. When the arrow is red, you must stop and cannot turn in that direction.

questions.question: What does a red flashing traffic light mean?

options.text: Solid red light.
Stop sign.
Yield sign.
Caution sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop. Then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Signal before going any further.
Slow down and yield for trains.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield for trains.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead. Slow down when you approach it. Trains cannot stop for cars, so you must wait for the train to pass before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill or incline with a curb, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
Keep your front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb when parking uphill. This stops your car from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.
Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.
Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: At a stop sign, after you stop, what should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars tailgating.
Move when the vehicle ahead of you moves.
Look right first, then left, then right again.
Look left first, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left first, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because vehicles from the left are closer to you. Then look right. Then look left again to check for any vehicles you may have missed.
